To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
young migrants, when asked to perform urban heritage sites, tend to perform them from a national perspective.

“The urban performance project, through the performance and re-enactment of heritage sites, allowed the young migrants to re-think their own belonging within the hosting nation, thus re-defining their sense of place and identity.”
“the urban unconscious of the nation is a frame of coexistence and not an identity bond”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how young migrants are able to make sense of the hosting nation and how they perform the nation in their everyday lives.
the ways in which the nation is being performed in the city by young migrants, as a way of negotiating the tensions between belonging, exclusion and inclusion, and between local and global.
the question of how the nation is experienced, performed and reconfigured in the city.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nation is not dead, and that the nation is alive in the city.
the urban nation can be thought of as an “urban unconscious”, a set of shared experiences that are not necessarily articulated in a discursive way.
the urban unconscious is the national unconscious, and that the urban is the nation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have tried to understand the nation as a set of shared experiences and not as a set of discourses.

the nation is not only a discursive and ideological construct but also an urban and emotional experience, and that the city is not only an arena of transnational encounter and diversity, but also an arena for the performance and negotiation of the nation.
the city is the nation, the nation is the city.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nation can be rethought as a space of co-existence, where the “us” is not defined by a common past, but by a shared future.
the urban scale can be a privileged site to explore the potentialities of a progressive notion of the nation.
, in the context of migration, the nation is a space that needs to be performed, rather than a given entity to be appropriated.
